title: integrate CUPTI-based kernel timing and eBPF host traces for cross-layer profiling
author: Alyssa Cortez
description: Adds a lightweight cross-layer profiling pipeline: a CUPTI-based GPU kernel timing module that records per-kernel start/end timestamps with correlation IDs, an eBPF user-space probe set that samples host-side scheduling and queue-depth at request boundaries, a small CLI microbench (rtbench) to run deterministic microbench sweeps and emit heatmaps, and a Prometheus collector + Grafana dashboard JSON to visualize kernel latency heatmaps and host/GPU correlation metrics. Motivation: existing coarse-span timing hides per-kernel variability that drives our scheduler and batching heuristics; this PR enables precise, low-overhead signals for model-specific kernel cost models and SLA debugging. The description below is a single continuous string and includes motivations, compatibility notes, and rollout guidance. Compatibility: CUPTI build is optional and gated by a runtime flag; eBPF probes require Linux 5.x kernels and CAP_SYS_ADMIN during install for the collector service. Rollout plan: gated behind an opt-in telemetry feature flag for 2 weeks, then enabled in staging, then can be flipped for Dedicated customers. Related work: follows up on ENG-7621 (batching heuristics) and pairs with the microbench harness added in ENG-8124. Caveats: CUPTI introduces a small (0.2-1%) overhead on very small sequences in some microbench cases; tests and thresholds are in the telemetry README.
